reason: Both correctly tell the homeowner to switch off and cool the oven, identify an SES/E14 heat-resistant oven lamp rated to 300°C, and neither mentions removing the glass lens cover or reading the old bulb's rating. Conversation 1 gives the exact matching spec (25W) and explicitly warns against using a normal household bulb, directly heading off the key unsupported claim. Conversation 2 adds a sensible escalation path (lamp holder/wiring -> engineer) but hedges with '25W or 40W', which could lead the homeowner to fit an over-wattage lamp in a holder specified for 25W, so its part advice is less precise. On balance Conversation 1's more accurate part recommendation slightly outweighs Conversation 2's better follow-up advice.
